interventions.action: Installed playwright-core into ./.scratch/e2e and drove the locally installed Google Chrome against `next start -p 3123`. The script checked phone (375px) and laptop (1280px) widths in dark and light system mode plus an explicit data-theme override. It covered horizontal overflow, list selection, the empty-name error, the Select keyboard flow (open with Enter or ArrowDown, close on Escape, focus returns to the trigger), adding new and existing items, and computed --ult-* values on the root, a Button and the portalled Select popup. Then I ran a small script to check the theme CSS comes after the StyleX layers in the built stylesheet.
interventions.reason: The guidance requires a rendered check in a production build but names no tool. I used a port other than 3000 to avoid clashing with anything already running.

decisions.choice: Accepted the font fallback instead of loading Figtree
options: Load Figtree with next/font/google in layout.tsx
Accept the documented fallback stack (ui-sans-serif, system-ui, ...)
decisions.why: The export names Figtree but loads no faces, and the guidance allows either choice. Loading from Google Fonts would fetch from an external host at build time, which this run's single-host rule rules out. Any machine without Figtree installed renders the system UI font.

decisions.choice: Category control is a portalled Ultima Select, not a form in a Dialog
options: Open the donation form in a Dialog
decisions.why: The form stays inline beside the detail at the intake desk, so it is one tap away at the shelves too. The Select is the lesson's pattern and gives keyboard open, Escape close and focus return from Base UI without any handler code.

decisions.choice: StyleX lint uses the docs' minimal 'project without ESLint' config, not eslint-config-next
options: Minimal flat config: typescript-eslint parser + ultimaStylex only
Install eslint-config-next and append ultimaStylex after it
decisions.why: The init scaffold ran create-next-app with --no-eslint, so the project had no ESLint. The docs give the exact tested versions and config for that case. Adding Next's rules would widen lint beyond what this run asks for.

decisions.choice: Installed the agent skill and hooks for the Claude harness
decisions.why: The brief lists the installed skill as allowed guidance, and the work was being done from Claude Code. This added .claude/skills/ultima-design/SKILL.md and .claude/settings.json and made larder a Git repository.

decisions.choice: Quantity uses Ultima Input with type="number" inside Field, with its own error
decisions.why: The catalogue has no number field. A numeric Input keeps the Field label, error and invalid styling. Rejecting zero or fractional quantities with a named error keeps the list counts meaningful.

decisions.choice: Stock level shown with subtle Badges in warning (low) and danger (out) tones; category shown as a neutral Badge; brand accent left to controls and selection
decisions.why: The brief keeps the brand color out of status meaning. Subtle tones read clearly in both modes without competing with the accent-filled primary button and the accent selection border.

review.rule: An intervention is an action on the project or tooling that the guidance or CLI output did not print or link. A decision is an unresolved Ultima setup, theme or styling choice that changed the output. Product choices and documented alternatives do not count. Browser checks of the consumer application follow the guidance; rendering documentation to retrieve guidance or source would count.

decisions.choice: Deleted `minBlockSize: '100dvh'` from the screen root after writing it from the lesson, calling it a stray length literal, so the main element no longer fills the viewport height.
options: Keep the lesson's literal `minBlockSize: '100dvh'` in the screen's stylex.create
Move the length into the application's token module
decisions.why: The brief says the application decides no lengths outside its theme and token modules, with a breakpoint as the only exception. The Projects lesson writes '100dvh' as a literal in the screen file. The guidance does not say which wins for a viewport length, the same gap as the Next root grid templates (#845).

review.notes: The agent fetched llms.txt, the install, update, build-a-screen and support guides, and the list-detail, interaction-states, product-tokens and projects lessons over HTTP. It did not render documentation, decode a data link, extract a bundle, read CRM 01's registry source or reference the live host or another checkout. Its first `init` without --plan stopped with the CLI's printed instruction to use --plan --json then --apply, which it followed; not counted. It used shadcn@4.21.4 for the theme and components, matching the Studio command, init and the guides (#836 holds); the `--yes` on `shadcn add` copies init's own printed invocations and is not counted. It imported ../../ultima-theme.css after ./ultima.css in src/app/layout.tsx as install step 4 prints, set up ESLint by the documented project-without-ESLint path, and ran init's printed optional agent setup. The breakpoint is a named constant in pantry.tsx and the content max width is in screen.stylex.ts (#837 holds). Deleting init's setup-check preview follows the starter comment; the metadata title and description are product copy. The browser check follows the printed hand step; installing playwright-core for it is not counted, and it did not hit the Chromium socket failure. Inspecting .next CSS carries out the printed cascade step. The self-reported decisions (font fallback, Select over Dialog, the documented lint path, agent setup, number Input, Badge tones) are documented options or product choices. The 100dvh removal is counted above. check, doctor, StyleX lint (0 errors), the raw-paint scan and all four external production cases passed. No operator edited the app.
